full_judgment: 42. Though the prosecution is not bound to call all available witnesses of accident irrespective of consideration, number or reliability witnesses essential to the unfolding of narrative on which prosecution is based must be called by the prosecution, whether in the result the effect of their testimony is for or against the case for the prosecution. It is a cardinal rule in the law of evidence that the best available evidence should be brought before the court to prove a fact or the points in issue. In the instant case the prosecution has withheld the eye witnesses and the injured passengers who are the vital witnesses. When material witnesses are not called in a case and no sufficient explanation has been given for their absence, the court may draw a presumption that they would not support the prosecution case. This view finds support of the decision in the case of Abdul Baher alias Abdul Baher and others vs. The state reported in 5 BLD 84 where in it has been held that prosecution is to call all the witnesses to prove the case and if all the witnesses are not called Without sufficient reason being shown, the court may draw adverse inference against the prosecution. Non-examination of witnesses mentioned in the charge sheet and FIR have weakened the prosecution case as such an adverse inference should reasonably be drawn against the prosecution. In the instant case, since all the eye witnesses have not been examined, so in the light of the above legal position and above decisions, adverse inference against the prosecution reasonably be drawn.
